# Repair cross-seat staff employment on load

## Goal

Repair saves that already contain player staff employed at another seat's business: on load the member is released from that business (employment cleared, removed from `employedStaff`, logged in the activity log), stays the player's hired staff, and the repair is idempotent across repeated load/save round-trips.

## Parent acceptance criteria covered

- A save already carrying player staff employed at another seat's business is repaired on load: the member is released from that business (employment cleared, removed from `employedStaff`, logged in the activity log), remains the player's hired staff, and the repair is idempotent across repeated load/save round-trips.

## Scope

- Add a load-time repair in `deserializeMainStreetState` (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`), after the existing per-business `employedStaff` backfill and before `attachMainStreetAchievements`, that walks `state.staffCards` and, for every member whose `employedAtSlot` points at a slot not owned by the member's owning seat, releases it:
  - remove the member from that business's `employedStaff` list;
  - clear `staff.employedAtSlot` (member remains in `staffCards`);
  - append an activity-log entry naming the member, the business and the seat it was released from.
- Determine the member's owning seat with the same rule as the engine: staff are player-only in competitive mode, so a member found at another seat's business belongs to seat 0 (`state.activePlayerId ?? 0` is not reliable across a loaded save; use the imported `getSlotOwnerId` plus the same acting-seat semantics used elsewhere — resolve this explicitly in the description of the change, preferring seat 0 as the human seat for legacy bad saves and documenting the choice in JSDoc).
- Keep the repair idempotent: a repaired state, re-serialised and re-loaded, produces no further activity-log entries and no further changes.
- Single-player / saves without `ownerTaggedGrid` are untouched.
- Add the JSDoc note explaining the repair and its idempotence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A save already carrying player staff employed at another seat's business is repaired on load: the member is released from that business (employment cleared, removed from `employedStaff`, logged in the activity log), remains the player's hired staff, and the repair is idempotent across repeated load/save round-trips.
- A single-player save and a save with no `ownerTaggedGrid` load unchanged (no repair, no activity-log entry).
- The repair is covered by a deterministic test that round-trips serialize → deserialize → serialize → deserialize and asserts exactly one activity-log entry.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a `repairCrossSeatStaffEmployment(state)` helper in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` and call it from `deserializeMainStreetState`.
2. Reuse `deregisterStaffFromSlot`-equivalent logic (or `removeStaffFromBusiness` where importable safely) and the activity-log append helper.
3. Run the child-1 save-repair test plus existing serialize/deserialize staff tests through `/skill:test`.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Staff ownership matrix tests (red).

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`
- `tests/main-street/staff-ownership-competitive.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/staff-movement.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts`

## Notes

- This implements assumption A3 (release, don't delete); if the producer rejects A3 the child is dropped without affecting the other children.
- Save-format change must stay backward compatible: older saves without owner tags load unchanged.


## Implementation decisions

- **Owning seat resolution.** Every member in `state.staffCards` belongs to the human seat (`STAFF_OWNING_SEAT_ID = 0`): staff are player-only in competitive play and salaries are charged from that one list, so a member found at another seat's business is unambiguously the player's. The repair therefore keys off slot ownership (`getSlotOwnerId`, the single shared predicate) against seat 0 — never `state.activePlayerId`, so a save captured mid-AI-turn repairs identically.
- **Release, not delete.** `employedAtSlot` is cleared, the member stays in `staffCards` (still hired, now unassigned) and every `employedStaff` reference to it is dropped, so the opponent's business stops resolving its buffs immediately.
- **Logged.** One seat-attributed activity-log entry (`addLog(state, 0, …)`) names the member and the business it was released from.
- **Idempotent.** A repaired state carries no `employedAtSlot` on the released member, so re-serialize → re-load writes nothing and logs nothing further.
- **Single-player unchanged.** The repair returns immediately when `ownerTaggedGrid` is absent; those saves load byte-identically with no log entry.

## Impact

A player who loads a save from before the ownership fix gets their staff member back as a hired-but-unassigned member instead of continuing to pay a salary that buffs an AI opponent's business.
data.title: Repair cross-seat staff employment on load

# Staff ownership docs and full suite

## Goal

Update the player-facing rules documentation and the remaining code-comment references so they state that staff placement, relocation and applicant targeting are restricted to the acting seat's own businesses, then verify the full project suite is green.

## Parent acceptance criteria covered

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (`MainStreetEngineCommands`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner`, `MainStreetStateSerialize` JSDoc), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (hire/relocate rule now states placement is restricted to the acting seat's own businesses), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (shared staff rules sentence), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Scope

- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — the hire/relocate rule (the action table rows and the relocation note) states that placement and relocation are restricted to the acting seat's own businesses in competitive play.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — the shared staff-rules sentence states the same restriction.
- Verify/complete the JSDoc in `MainStreetEngineCommands` (applicant + placement/relocation helpers), `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner` (staff gate reference) and `MainStreetStateSerialize` (load-time repair) — the implementation children add their own JSDoc, so this child only needs to close any remaining gaps and keep the wording consistent with the docs.
- Scan for relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/` pages beyond the two named, any wiki vault linked from the repo) and update them where they describe staff placement/relocation.
- Run the full project suite through `/skill:test` and triage any failures into critical `test-failure` items per the triage policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (`MainStreetEngineCommands`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner`, `MainStreetStateSerialize` JSDoc), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (hire/relocate rule now states placement is restricted to the acting seat's own businesses), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (shared staff rules sentence), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Update the two named docs pages and any wiki/docs-site entries found.
2. Close JSDoc gaps left by the implementation children.
3. Run `/skill:test` (full suite) and confirm green; triage any failures.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Gate staff placement on slot ownership.
- Depends on: Ownership-aware staff applicant resolution.
- Depends on: Repair cross-seat staff employment on load.

## Key Files

- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`

## Notes

- Keep the docs wording consistent with the engine rejection message (`That business belongs to <seat>.`).
- Do not re-document the unchanged salary model, 1-action relocation cost or two-type staff model.

# Action classification for Summary tab

Add an optional `action` property to the `LogEntry` type and set it at every player- and AI-initiated action `addLog` call site. Turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows deliberately leave it unset, so the Summary tab can structurally distinguish action rows from summary rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Action classification is structural, not textual: the turn record exposes an explicit action marker (an optional category on `LogEntry`, set wherever a player- or AI-initiated action is logged), so no rendered action row depends on matching log message text.
- `LogEntry` in `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` carries an optional `action` field (a string categorising the action type).
- Every `addLog` call site that records a player- or AI-initiated action (placing a business, hiring staff, playing an upgrade/event, moving a card to hand, selling, laying off, closing a street card, loans, challenge completions) sets the `action` field to a consistent category string.
- Turn headers and per-turn monetary summary rows (income/reputation lines) carry no `action` marker.
- A guard test asserts that every known action-producing `addLog` call site sets the marker, catching regressions.
- All existing tests pass.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add optional `action` to `LogEntry`
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` and all `addLog` call sites — set the marker at action sites
- `tests/main-street/log-entry-action-marker.test.ts` — guard test

## Minimal Implementation
- Add optional `action?: string` to the `LogEntry` interface.
- Enumerate action category constants for each action type.
- Set the `action` field at each `addLog` call site that records a player- or AI-initiated action.
- Leave turn headers and monetary summary rows unset.

## Deliverables
- Updated `LogEntry` type, marked call sites, guard test.

## Dependencies
None — this is a foundational, additive change.
data.title: Add LogEntry action marker and set at call sites
